source.statement: This contract is derived from Broadcom's rendered xAPIs reference documentation for VCF Automation, not from a published API specification. VCF Automation has no specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository and no generated VMware.Sdk.Vcf.* PowerCLI binding, so no machine-readable artifact exists to project from. Every operation, parameter, property and enumeration below was transcribed by hand from the reference pages recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Treat it as a focused transcription of documentation, not as a normative schema: the reference pages are the authority, and anything they do not state is deliberately absent here.
apiProducts: VCF Automation API - VM Apps Org - Catalog
VCF Automation API - VM Apps Org - Deployment
source.operationIdAvailability: The xAPIs reference pages publish a summary and a method/path for each operation but do not publish an operationId. The operationKey values in this contract are therefore contract-local identifiers coined for this projection; they are not vendor identifiers and must not be presented as such.

authentication.tokenAcquisition: Out of scope for this contract. The reference pages document the data-plane operations below and state only that they require bearerAuth; no token-issuing operation is projected here.

operations.summary: Creates a deployment from a catalog item.

focusedWireProfile.notes: A conditional member is serialized exactly when the caller explicitly binds it, including an explicitly supplied empty string or empty object. An unbound member is absent from the JSON object: not null, not an empty string, not an empty object and not a default number.

200.description: The blueprint service's response to a deployment request.

parameters.name: expandResources
parameters.description: The 'resources' field of the deployment will be retrieved.

parameters.name: expandProject
parameters.description: The 'project' field of the deployment will be retrieved.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: The expanded details of the requested comma separated objects. 'resources' option returns resources with all properties. Ex. blueprint, project

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Retrieves the deployment, includes soft-deleted deployments that have not yet been completely deleted.

focusedWireProfile.notes: expandLastRequest is bound to the literal value true so that the response carries the lastRequest object. Every other optional query member is absent from the query string, not present-and-false and not present-and-empty.

operations.summary: Get the Request. Returns the request with the given ID.

focusedWireProfile.notes: The poll is a bare bodyless GET and carries no query string.

operations.summary: Submit action on requests. Allowable values: cancel, dismiss.
operations.description: Cancel can be submitted on In-progress requests and Dismiss can be submitted on Failed requests.

focusedWireProfile.notes: The reference page documents no request body for this operation. The request is sent with no body at all; an empty JSON object must not be sent in its place.

200.description: OK. Operation doesn't return any data structure.

bulkRequestCount.description: Deployment request count; defaults to 1 if not specified.

projectId.description: Project to be used for the request

version.description: Version of the catalog item. e.g. v2.0

CatalogItemRequest.notes: The reference page marks every member optional. Optionality is not permission to serialize a member the caller never set.

CatalogItemRequestResponseItemArray.notes: The reference page documents only deploymentId and deploymentName on the response item. It carries no request identifier, so the identifier of the asynchronous request that fulfils the deployment must be discovered through getDeploymentById.

Deployment.notes: lastRequest is the Request object for the deployment's most recent request and is populated only when expandLastRequest is bound. inprogressRequests is documented only as an object named inprogressRequests; the reference page specifies neither its element shape nor its ordering, so it is not a dependable source for the request identifier. The deployment status is the status of the deployment, not of the request, and reaching a terminal request status is not the same as the deployment status changing.

approvedAt.description: Time at which the request was approved

blueprintId.description: Identifier of the requested blueprint in the form 'UUID:version'

cancelable.description: Indicates whether request can be canceled or not

catalogItemId.description: Identifier of the requested catalog item in the form 'UUID:version'

completedAt.description: Time at which the request completed

completedTasks.description: The number of tasks completed while fulfilling this request

deploymentId.description: Identifier of the requested deployment id

details.description: Longer user-friendly details of the request

dismissed.description: Indicates whether request is in dismissed state

initializedAt.description: Time at which the request was initialized

name.description: Short user-friendly label of the request (e.g. 'shuting down myVM')

resourceIds.description: Optional resource ids to which the request applies to

totalTasks.description: The total number of tasks need to be completed to fulfil this request

asynchronousProfile.statement: requestCatalogItem is asynchronous. A 200 from it means the request was accepted, not that the deployment exists or succeeded. The request identifier is not in that response and must be read from the deployment's lastRequest, then polled with getRequestById until the request status is terminal.

requestStatusClassification.notes: The documented spelling of the in-progress status is INPROGRESS with no separator. COMPLETION is a stage on the way to a terminal status, not a terminal status. Any status outside this enumeration is unknown and must not be treated as success.

cancellation.notes: The reference page states that cancel can be submitted on in-progress requests. The Request object's cancelable member indicates whether the request can be canceled; a request whose most recent poll reported cancelable false must not be sent a cancel.
